allowed_dependency_manifest.content: For each fixed integer n greater than 1, define f_n(x) = floor of (n times x) minus the sum for k from 1 to n of (floor of (k times x) divided by k). Determine the set of real x that maximize f_n(x) over all real numbers x, and determine the maximum value of f_n(x).

forbidden_claims.label: root_theorem_claim
forbidden_claims.reason: root theorem proposition is not citable solver context
forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer greater than 1. For which real numbers $x$ is \\[\\lfloor nx \\rfloor - \\sum_{k=1}^{n} \\frac{\\lfloor kx \\rfloor}{k}\\] maximal, and what is the maximal value that this expression can take?

payload.role_in_assembly: Show that on each early interval, the maximum is attained at the left endpoint m/n.

domain_restrictions: n is an integer greater than 1
k is an integer with 1 less than or equal to k less than or equal to n
x ranges over all real numbers
floor is the usual greatest integer function mapping real inputs to integers
root_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For each fixed integer n greater than 1, define f_n(x) = floor of (n times x) minus the sum for k from 1 to n of (floor of (k times x) divided by k). Determine the set of real x that maximize f_n(x) over all real numbers x, and determine the maximum value of f_n(x).
quantifier_order: Fix an integer n with n greater than 1
There exists a real x such that the expression at x is at least the expression at every real y
For all real y, compare the expression value at x versus y

variables.name: n
variables.role: fixed parameter used in the definition of the objective function and in the summation range

variables.name: x
variables.role: free variable over which the expression is maximized

variables.name: k
variables.role: summation index ranging from 1 to n

witness_dependencies: The maximizing real number(s) x can depend on the chosen integer n
The claimed maximal value depends on n

domain_restrictions: the comparisons F_n(y) <= F_n(x) are meaningful, so outputs of F_n are in an orderable domain
semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: Fix an integer n. For every integer m with 0 <= m <= n-2, and for all real numbers x and y in [m/n, (m+1)/n) with x <= y, the inequality F_n(y) <= F_n(x) holds.
quantifier_order: for every integer m such that 0 <= m <= n-2
for all real numbers x and y such that x and y lie in [m/n, (m+1)/n) and x <= y

variables.name: n
variables.role: global parameter indexing the function F_n and the partition size

variables.name: x
variables.role: left argument point in the subinterval

variables.name: y
variables.role: right argument point in the subinterval

variables.domain: at least defined on every real number in the union of intervals [m/n, (m+1)/n) for allowed m
variables.name: F_n
variables.role: maps inputs x to outputs F_n(x) that can be compared with <= (belonging to a totally ordered set)

witness_dependencies: No existential witnesses are introduced; the universal conditions quantify x and y directly within the same chosen interval determined by m

payload.statement_nl: For every integer m with 0 <= m <= n-2, the function F_n is nonincreasing on the interval [m/n, (m+1)/n): if x and y lie in this interval and x <= y, then F_n(y) <= F_n(x).
